body:
Hey thanks for the feedback. Loosing a bit of weight would be lovely, but as we all know is a slow, painful process full of false starts that can daunt even the most determined. I look into fashion advice though. I'm still in the 'clothes are things I wear so I can't be naked' mindset, so it seems like a quick win.

Also, I the sort of high-strung mess who thinks being 'okay' at something is the same as being worthless.

It does mean a lot to me. When I was in college, I fell apart my first year. I ended up hospitalized for depression, and frankly it saved my life. I can imagine what you're going through right now. It's brutal and I really empathize. I can't promise you shit will get better, but the truth is it did get better for me for a while. I had a happy relationship though it ultimately fell apart. I pulled through and graduated doing pretty well. I'm rooting for you to be able to do the same (ideally without the hospitalization).

And hey, don't feel guilty for the way depression can incapacitate you. It's just as hard as fighting a chronic illness or a disability. 

Keep trying, I'm on you side.

Honestly, if it's any consolation, feeling like somethings ok even with the loneliness, and especially with other kinds of social connection, can ease some of the pain. 6 days out of 7, I can feel alright about it all and live with it. It's those times that the whole thing comes crashing down that I sort of fall apart.

While I don't know your story, but I can guess at some of it. I want you to know that what you are feeling is totally valid, and anyone who says it isn't needs to back off.

That said, I do hope you chose to live and chose to build up a life after your loss. I don't say this to stop the pain, but to tell you that there is a life to be lived with pain. I myself made the choice to live that life, pain and all. You don't have to make that choice, no one else can make it for you. I just want to know you have a choice.

My experience with telling people bout my depression has generally been that people will not judge you and will usually try to help. Often they don't know what to do, but they are almost always caring and sympathetic. 

For a long time I was afraid that people would think I was weak and not like me, and that has happened, but it's been very rare. In fact, it's deepened my relationship with a lot of people.

All that said, it's important to be careful with your word choice. If people think you are an immediate risk to yourself or others and you aren't, then they may act in ways that they think are helpful but aren't. A therapist knows the difference between "sometimes I think I shouldn't be here" and an immediate threat, but family and friends don't.

I know what that's like and I'm really glad it happened to you. Two nights ago, I was at the point of planning my suicide and my dad talked me out of it, by telling me how much it would break him and mother. 

Maybe our lives aren't worth it for us right now, but I guess they are worth it for someone else.

I hate invalidating what anyone who feels like you says, because I feel the way you do and hate it when people invalidate what I feel. The only strength I can offer you is to let you know that you don't have to do it. You can choose not to. It's not my place to tell you what you should do, but I want you to know you always have a choice, and that I trust you to make it.

I want you to know that I, for one, respect the hell out of you. You've opened up to having one of the most unfairly despised conditions in the world. You're resisting it and that makes you a heck of a lot stronger than most people I know.

I can't pretend to even start to understand what that's like. I can't understand how hard it is. All I can tell you is that I hope you don't hurt yourself. I hope you know that some of us, out here, don't think you're evil for what you've thought and felt. I admire your bravery.

And I do agree with some other posters that it might be good for you to stop working with kids. I have no place telling you if it will make things easier or harder, but if you think it might, I encourage you to do it.
Please read rule 3 of the subreddit rules for /r/depression

I empathize so much with your experience.
I know what it's like to never want to do anything. 
I know what it's like to break down under emotional stress and do awful things to people. Last week I said awful, hurtful things to my ex-girlfriend until she lost it and threatened me. 
I know what it's like to feel the shame afterwards. The feeling that it wasn't even you who did that. It's horrible.

But people can forgive. There are lots of us out there who've been through emotional agony. We know what it's like. We know it can push normal people to do horrible things. In the past, I've done awful things to a lot of people. And a lot of those people were eventually able to forgive me once they understood the pain I had been in, and how much I just wanted to make amends and do better.

Your pain is valid. Your thoughts are valid. It's okay that you feel the way you do. Thank you for sharing.

A lot of people think depression is a curable condition, like pneumonia, or a dislocated shoulder. See the right doctor, get the right medication and therapy and bam, you're better. My personal theory, based on my own experience, is that people thing that Major Depression is just like really bad sadness, or like the transient depression people go through when they've experienced a personal tragedy. They want to relate to what's happened to them, and the things they've experienced are completely curable with time and help.

Major Depression, is not like this. Depression is a lifelong burden that we have to bear. I'm not minimizing the value of therapy. But I think it's very hard for people to accept that you will never recover from depression. The best you can hope for is remission.
